articles.title: No Reflow at Perfusion Imaging: Thresholds That Distinguish Functional and Tissue Outcome Groups in Acute Stroke.
articles.abstract: Background Poor outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) may reflect microvascular dysfunction, or no-reflow phenomenon, but operational definitions are lacking. Purpose To identify the most informative candidate no-reflow definition at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging for outcome assessment. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis used data from two prospective multicenter imaging registries of patients with acute stroke who were recruited between June 2016 and July 2022, achieved modified thrombolysis in cerebral infarction grade 2c or 3 recanalization after EVT, and underwent pre-EVT and 24-hour post-EVT CT or MR perfusion imaging. Candidate no-reflow definitions were evaluated across eight perfusion maps and their corresponding stepwise thresholds. Delay time (DT) quantifies the delay in contrast material arrival between arterial input and brain tissue. For primary screening, no-reflow status was defined as any residual hypoperfusion lesion for each map-threshold combination. The best-performing combination was evaluated using residual volume and reperfusion index cutoffs. The primary outcome was poor 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score >2); infarct growth was secondary. Associations with the outcome were evaluated using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression. Results The primary cohort included 67 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 56-77 years]; 41 male), and the independent cohort comprised 54 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 62-78 years]; 28 female). In the primary cohort, lesions with DT longer than 4 seconds showed the strongest discrimination for poor 90-day functional outcome (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.72 [95% CI: 0.57, 0.86]; P < .001). According to this definition, 14 of 67 patients (21%) had no reflow. Poor functional outcome occurred in 11 of 14 patients (79%) with no reflow and 11 of 53 (21%) with reflow (odds ratio, 12.14 [95% CI: 3.38, 54.63]; P < .001). Infarct growth was greater with no-reflow status than with reflow (median, 24.1 mL [IQR, 3.7-40.7 mL] vs 0 mL [IQR, -10.1 to 6.1 mL]; P < .001). Findings were consistent in the independent cohort. Conclusion The presence of a lesion with DT longer than 4 seconds at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging appeared to be the most informative candidate no-reflow definition. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Gemmete in this issue.

articles.title: How I Do It: An Imaging Approach and Review of Autoimmune Encephalitis.
articles.abstract: Encephalitis is a medical emergency characterized by inflammation of the brain parenchyma due to an infective cause or an immune-mediated process. Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) is characterized by a misdirected immune attack against neuronal structures, resulting in an inflammatory response. Triggers for the development of antibodies are often paraneoplastic or parainfectious. AE may occur in children or adults with symptoms including subacute onset of altered mentation, cognitive issues, drug-resistant epilepsy, movement disorders, and/or autonomic dysfunction. Limbic encephalitis is a common imaging feature of many forms of AE; however, cortical, basal ganglia, diencephalon, brainstem, and cerebellar involvement have been described. This article provides an overview of the general imaging appearances of AE, with a detailed discussion of key patterns encountered with common causes of AE, as well as a review of the relevant differential diagnoses, thus serving as a practical reference for radiologists.

articles.title: Intraindividual Comparison of Radiation Dose and Image Quality: Photon-counting versus Energy-integrating Detector CT in Obesity.
articles.abstract: Background Maintaining diagnostic CT image quality in patients with obesity remains challenging because increased x-ray attenuation is often offset by higher radiation exposure. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) has demonstrated improved dose efficiency and image quality, but intraindividual data in this population are limited. Purpose To compare radiation dose, quantitative image quality, and subjective image quality between PCCT and energy-integrating detector (EID) CT intraindividually in patients with obesity. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with obesity undergoing thoracic and/or abdominal CT at both PCCT and EID CT between December 1, 2022, and January 31, 2025. Signal, image noise, and signal to noise ratio (SNR) were measured in vascular, parenchymal, muscular, and adipose tissue. Two radiologists independently rated image quality on a six-point Likert scale. Radiation dose parameters were volume CT dose index (CTDIvol), dose-length product (DLP), and effective dose. The paired two-sided t test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for group comparisons. Results This study included 51 patients with obesity (median age, 56 years [IQR, 51-66.5 years]; 33 male). Signal was higher with PCCT than EID CT in vascular structures, parenchymal organs, and muscle and more negative in subcutaneous fat (all P < .001), with similar image noise (P = .09-.84). SNR was higher with PCCT in vascular structures (ascending aorta: mean, 19.65 ± 6.47 [SD] vs 13.22 ± 4.83; P < .001) and most parenchymal organs (liver: 5.53 ± 1.69 vs 4.71 ± 1.89; P = .02). The difference in SNR increased with body mass index for vessels (r = 0.36) and parenchymal organs (r = 0.51) (both P < .001). Both readers rated overall image quality, contrast, and sharpness higher and artifact-related impairment lower for PCCT (all P < .001), whereas subjective image noise was similar (P = .16 and .14). CTDIvol (median, 11.99 vs 17.05 mGy) and DLP (median, 526.25 vs 709.32 mGy · cm) were lower with PCCT (both P < .001). Conclusion In patients with obesity, intraindividual comparisons demonstrated that PCCT had superior quantitative and subjective image quality at a lower radiation dose than EID CT. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Redistribution of Pulmonary Vascular Volume at Upright versus Supine CT.
articles.abstract: Background Gravity redistributes pulmonary blood flow in the upright position; however, how total pulmonary vascular volume (TPVV) and its arterial and venous components depend on position remains unclear. Purpose To quantify position-dependent changes in TPVV and the corresponding arterial and venous components across lung lobes and vertical lung regions using upright chest CT. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis of a prospective, single-center study enrolled healthy adult volunteers who underwent same-day noncontrast chest CT in supine and upright positions using a 320-detector row CT system between March 2018 and December 2018. Participants were excluded for incidental lung abnormalities or inadequate vessel separation. Pulmonary arteries and veins were segmented semiautomatically, and pulmonary vascular volumes were quantified for whole lung, lobes, and upper, middle, and lower lung regions. Paired two-sided t tests with Bonferroni correction were used for comparisons. Results Fifty participants (mean age ± SD, 47 years ± 9.7; 28 men) were evaluated. Standing reduced TPVV by 18.8% compared with the supine position (mean, 99.8 mL ± 18.2 vs 81.0 mL ± 14.3; P < .001). When standing, pulmonary venous volume decreased more than pulmonary arterial volume across the whole lung (25.4% reduction [mean, 50.7 mL ± 9.1 supine vs 37.5 mL ± 5.7 standing] vs 11.1% reduction [mean, 49.1 mL ± 9.9 supine vs 43.6 mL ± 9.4 standing]; P < .001). Volume reductions when standing followed a craniocaudal gradient, with greater reductions in the upper lung than in the lower lung (P < .001). Dependent lower lung regions also showed decreases in TPVV (mean reduction, -12.0%; mean, 40.4 mL ± 9.0 supine vs 35.4 mL ± 7.7 standing), pulmonary arterial volume (mean reduction, -6.0%; mean, 18.2 mL ± 3.9 supine vs 17.1 mL ± 4.5 standing), and pulmonary venous volume (mean reduction, -16.7%; mean, 22.2 mL ± 4.6 supine vs 18.3 mL ± 3.7 standing; all P < .001). Conclusion Upright chest CT showed that, compared with the supine position, standing reduced TPVV, predominantly venous, with a vertical gradient, where dependent lower lung regions exhibited modest volume reduction. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Suh in this issue.

Provider and patient perceptions on the usage of whole-body magnetic resonance imaging in oncology: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: Whole-body MRI (WB-MRI) is increasingly used for early diagnosis, cancer staging and treatment monitoring, but adoption remains sub-optimal. The aim of this scoping review was to map research on patient and provider perspectives of WB-MRI in oncology, and identify methodological limitations and evidence gaps. The review followed the JBI methodological framework and the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Five electronic databases were searched from inception to 29th March 2025: Cochrane Library, PubMed, APA PsycINFO, APA Psych Articles, and Academic Search Complete. Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed by two authors independently, using COVIDENCE software, with results summarized via narrative synthesis. Twenty-eight studies met eligibility criteria, covering four distinct populations: general population (n = 8), people with cancer pre-disposition syndromes (n = 7), or suspected or confirmed cancer (n = 10), and radiologists (n = 3). Few studies examined beliefs about WB-MRI. Limited evidence shows awareness of WB-MRI attributes, such as the absence of ionising radiation, predicts preferences among cancer patients. Research on radiologists shows low levels of WB-MRI adoption in the USA and UK, attributed to limited scanner availability and a lack of trained radiologists. Among patients, uptake is modest (60%) in both population cohort studies and those recommended for surveillance, but the role of scan beliefs in predicting uptake has not been explored. Undergoing WB-MRI, or being notified of incidental findings, does not appear to cause adverse psychological consequences, but cancer specific concerns were not always assessed and research not always adequately powered. Evidence of provider and patient perspectives towards WB-MRI is limited and of varying quality. The development of validated measures examining WB-MRI beliefs and experience would enhance research and facilitate future data synthesis.Clinical trial number Not applicable.

articles.title: M4DTrack: A DICOM-Based Imaging Informatics Workflow for User-Supervised 4DCT Lung Tumor Motion Reporting.
articles.abstract: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is routinely used in radiotherapy simulation to evaluate respiration-induced tumor motion, but the motion information is often reviewed visually rather than captured as structured, phase-resolved data. We developed and evaluated M4DTrack, a DICOM-based imaging-informatics workflow for user-supervised 4DCT lung tumor motion analysis and structured, exportable three-dimensional center-of-mass (CoM) motion reporting. M4DTrack imports phase-resolved DICOM CT images, groups images by respiratory phase, displays linked axial/coronal/sagittal views, supports crosshair-based tumor localization and HU inspection, and applies seed or linked 3D-box initialization with sequential phase-to-phase HU-volume propagation. An 8-case lower-lobe lung 4DCT dataset (80 respiratory phases) was analyzed. Directional amplitudes, 3D vector amplitude, maximum phase-wise displacement, and agreement with independent ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were quantified. HU-weighted CoM amplitudes were 2.44 ± 1.44 mm, 2.64 ± 1.37 mm, and 6.04 ± 2.48 mm in X, Y, and Z patient-coordinate directions, respectively. Mean 3D vector amplitude was 7.26 ± 2.50 mm, and mean maximum phase-wise 3D displacement was 6.20 ± 2.10 mm. Biases versus ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were 0.01, - 0.84, and 0.23 mm for X, Y, and Z, respectively, with a 3D vector amplitude bias of - 0.29 mm. M4DTrack provides a user-supervised imaging-informatics bridge between qualitative 4DCT cine review and structured quantitative motion documentation. The pilot results support feasibility for generating exportable, phase-resolved tumor-motion metrics while preserving user-supervised review of 4DCT artifacts, HU-capture uncertainty, adjacent anatomy, and differences between CoM-based and extent-based measurements.

articles.title: 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN: Pulmonary Nodule Detection Through Cross-Slice Feature Fusion and Dynamic Displacement Modeling.
articles.abstract: Accurate pulmonary nodule detection in computed tomography (CT) remains challenging because small- and low-contrast nodules may resemble vessels and other anatomical structures on individual axial slices. We propose 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN, a multi-slice detection framework that incorporates structured local axial context into a two-stage detector. The five-slice interactive blending (5-SIB) strategy organizes five consecutive CT slices as an ordered contextual group and preserves slice-specific feature streams extracted by a shared two-dimensional backbone. The cross-slice feature fusion (CSFF) module applies slice-wise spatial self-attention at shallow feature levels and learnable cross-slice aggregation at deep feature and region-of-interest levels. The dynamic displacement constraint (DDC) models proposal displacement across adjacent slices using a positive-sample regression loss and a margin-based negative-sample contrastive loss, while a class-weighted focal loss alleviates foreground-background imbalance. The model was evaluated on a private hospital dataset, LIDC-IDRI, and LNDb using patient-level data partitions. On the private hospital dataset, 3D-DDN achieved an average precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5 (AP0.5) of 75.80% ± 1.05%, a sensitivity of 89.33% ± 1.91%, and a competition performance metric (CPM) of 91.20% ± 1.50%. The corresponding AP0.5 values on LIDC-IDRI and LNDb were 66.27% ± 0.45% and 48.20% ± 0.30%, respectively. Ablation experiments showed that direct five-slice stacking degraded performance, whereas structured feature fusion and displacement supervision recovered the performance loss and improved the overall detection profile. These results indicate that ordered cross-slice representation, hierarchical feature fusion, and proposal-displacement supervision provide complementary mechanisms for incorporating local three-dimensional context.

articles.title: Operational Ontology for Radiology: A Framework for Profiling and Characterizing CT Imaging Data.
articles.abstract: Medical imaging data are increasingly used for benchmarking, quality improvement, research, and artificial intelligence applications. However, the lack of consistent metadata characterization limits the reliability and scalability of such analyses. Existing standards provide syntactic interoperability but often fail to capture the semantic clinical context and workflow details necessary for secondary uses such as AI development and radiation safety assessment, affecting the utility for reproducible profiling of imaging examinations across institutions. In this work, we describe key gaps in current approaches to imaging data standardization. These include syntactic interoperability without semantic equivalence, limited representation of clinically relevant context, inconsistent definitions of radiology procedures across institutions, and the absence of mechanisms to systematically profile imaging examinations for analysis. These limitations make it difficult to compare imaging practices, aggregate datasets, and interpret results across sites. To address these challenges, we have devised an ontology framework, the Operational Ontology for Radiology (OOR), that models the radiology study workflow from ordering through interpretation using explicitly defined entities, relationships, and annotated data properties. A CT-focused implementation of the framework was then formed, including 34 classes, 15 object properties, and 156 data properties in this present formation. The framework was deployed in a demonstrative use case scenario to illustrate the utility of OOR in drawing more clinically relevant radiation dose aggregates from clinical CT data. The work demonstrates that OOR provides both a structured representation of imaging data and a foundation for more transparent data aggregation, scalable secondary analysis, and reproducible characterization of imaging practices across institutions.

articles.title: TurkRadLLM: A Compact MedGemma-Based Model for Structuring Turkish Lumbar and Cervical Spine MRI Reports-A Multi-reader Validation Study.
articles.abstract: To develop and validate a compact, locally deployable MedGemma-based model converting unstructured Turkish spine MRI reports into structured six-field output. In this retrospective single-institution study, 5210 lumbar and 5017 cervical Turkish spine MRI reports were used to fine-tune MedGemma 4B IT with QLoRA. Silver-standard labels from a proprietary large language model served as training targets and as the reference for automated fidelity analyses, but not as the clinical reference standard. Evaluation comprised multi-reader validation of 180 authentic reports interleaved with 20 adversarial cases, a second round in which the readers scored the silver labels themselves, and comparison on the full held-out set against a rule-based baseline, the non-fine-tuned base model, and a much larger model. Every output was valid, schema-conformant JSON, and the grouped acceptance rate was 100% (95% CI 97.9-100), though one reader judged negative-finding lists incomplete in 57.8% of reports. On the full held-out set (1025 reports), fine-tuning increased agreement with the silver-label impression from 17.7% to 67.1% and urgent-flag sensitivity against the silver reference from 18.8% to 62.5% (both p < .001); the larger non-fine-tuned model reached 27.5% and 50.0%, and a rule-based baseline 99.0% on body region. When the readers scored the silver labels themselves, the model was rated higher on negative findings and lower on the impression. Deployment required 14.75 GB of GPU memory on a consumer card. Fine-tuning a compact medical language model produced structured output rated acceptable by clinicians, though negative-finding completeness remained reader-dependent. The gain lay in content-level fidelity rather than output validity.

articles.title: ASFNR Clinical State of Practice Statement on Imaging of Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking. METHODS: The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature. KEY MESSAGE: Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.

articles.title: Sagittal spinopelvic parameters in children and adolescents: a retrospective cross-sectional radiographic study from Turkey.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sagittal spinal parameters are used to assess upright alignment during growth. OBJECTIVE: To describe sagittal spinopelvic parameters and assess their associations with age and sex in children and adolescents in Turkey. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study at a single tertiary orthopedic center included 344 children aged 6-17 years (186 boys, 158 girls) who underwent clinically indicated standing full-spine radiography. Pelvic incidence, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, lumbar lordosis, thoracic kyphosis, sagittal vertical axis, cervical vertebra (C) 2 tilt, thoracic vertebra (T) 4 tilt, lumbar vertebra (L) 1 tilt, T4 pelvic angle, and L1 pelvic angle were assessed. Age-group comparisons and age- and sex-adjusted linear models were used. RESULTS: Mean (standard deviation) pelvic incidence, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, lumbar lordosis, and thoracic kyphosis were 45.4 (12.3)°, 11.3 (6.9)°, 34.2 (10.4)°, 57.5 (13.8)°, and 46.0 (13.4)°, respectively; sagittal vertical axis was 46.6 (27.6) mm. C2, T4, and L1 tilts were 5.0 (2.9)°, 10.4 (4.6)°, and 9.0 (4.7)°; T4 pelvic angle and L1 pelvic angle were 4.1 (3.1)° and 3.4 (3.1)°. Lumbar lordosis showed the largest adjusted age coefficient (1.81°/year; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.28-2.34; adjusted R2=0.121). T4 pelvic angle and L1 pelvic angle did not differ significantly across age groups (P=0.308 and P=0.966). CONCLUSION: In children and adolescents without radiographic spinal or pelvic deformity, lumbar lordosis had the clearest cross-sectional association with age. No statistically significant age-group differences were detected for T4 pelvic angle or L1 pelvic angle. These data provide clinically relevant standing-radiograph reference data for sagittal spinopelvic parameters.

articles.title: An enlarged nonfistulous artery mimicking an additional feeder in a pediatric pial arteriovenous fistula: an angiographic pitfall.
articles.abstract: Pial arteriovenous fistulas (PAVFs) are rare high-flow vascular lesions requiring precise characterization of the fistulous angioarchitecture before treatment. We report a pediatric PAVF in which an enlarged artery adjacent to the fistula initially appeared suspicious for additional fistulous supply. Superselective angiography demonstrated normal cortical arterial arborization and parenchymal perfusion without early venous drainage, confirming that the enlarged vessel did not participate directly in the arteriovenous shunt. Selective coil embolization achieved complete immediate occlusion of the fistulous communication while preserving the adjacent normal cortical arterial supply. This case illustrates that arterial enlargement alone does not establish participation in a PAVF and highlights an angiographic pitfall relevant to treatment planning.

articles.title: Machine learning-based CT radiomics for identifying high risk esophageal varices of bleeding in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in patients with HCC. METHODS: 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics. CONCLUSION: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

articles.title: Automated virtual reduction of pseudo-fractured mandibles using sex-specific statistical shape models: a proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This proof-of-concept study developed an automated virtual mandibular fracture reduction framework using statistical shape models (SSMs), evaluated it in ten controlled pseudo-fracture cases, and compared sex-specific and combined-sex SSMs. METHODS: Male, female, and combined-sex SSMs were constructed from CT-derived mandibular meshes using the same correspondence estimation, atlas updating, and principal component analysis pipeline. Ten independent mandibles (five male and five female) were divided into three fragments and displaced. Reduction jointly optimized SSM coefficients and fragment transformations using the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy. Paired results were compared using exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: The male, female, and combined-sex SSMs required 28, 32, and 29 principal components, respectively, to reach 95% cumulative explained variance. Using the sex-specific SSMs, the mean symmetric chamfer distance and symmetric root-mean-square error were 0.712 ± 0.210 mm and 0.855 ± 0.231 mm, respectively, compared with 0.778 ± 0.309 mm and 0.937 ± 0.358 mm using the combined-sex SSM. Although the sex-specific SSMs yielded numerically lower mean errors, the differences were not statistically significant (p = 0.232 and p = 0.193, respectively). Computation time was approximately 23 min per reduction run. CONCLUSION: The framework achieved near-millimetric accuracy, supporting the technical feasibility of automated virtual mandibular reduction under controlled conditions. Sex-specific SSMs yielded numerically lower errors than the combined-sex SSM, without a statistically significant advantage. Larger validation cohorts and real-fracture studies are required before clinical application.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Age- and sex-specific values of regional bone mineral density from opportunistic CT of the lower lumbar spine, pelvis, sacrum, and proximal femur.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Standard osteoporosis assessment using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) provides limited 2D measures (BMD, T-score), potentially missing localized bone density differences relevant to fracture risk. Opportunistic CT allows comprehensive 3D volumetric bone density analysis. This study presents a detailed 3D statistical model of CT-derived apparent volumetric bone mineral density (CT-vBMD) covering the L4 and L5 vertebrae, pelvic bones, sacrum, and proximal femur and examines spatial distributions and associations with age and sex. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis included 330 routine abdominal CT scans (ages 20-91; approximately balanced by sex). Bones were segmented with a semi-automated workflow, internally calibrated, registered to bone-specific population templates, and projected onto corresponding tetrahedral meshes. Whole-bone averages were compared across age groups and between sexes. For each element, we calculated mean vBMD, variability, correlations with age and sex, and cluster-defined low-density and age-sensitive subregions. RESULTS: The global spatial pattern was similar in females and males. The highest CT-vBMD values were localized mainly to cortical load-bearing zones, whereas the lowest values were concentrated in trabecular spongiosa. Older age was associated with lower whole-bone CT-vBMD in all bones and with stronger negative associations in trabecular-rich regions, such as the subchondral acetabulum, femoral neck, sacral ala, and vertebral bodies. Cortical-dominant load-bearing regions showed weaker negative associations with age. CONCLUSION: This framework maps anatomically localized associations between age and CT-vBMD beyond the regions routinely assessed by DXA. Opportunistic CT mapping may complement standard osteoporosis assessment by providing spatial information for the pelvis, sacrum, lower lumbar spine, and proximal femur.

articles.title: Nonlinear stability phenotypes and collapse dynamics of multi-organ radiomics in total-body PET imaging: toward digital twin-oriented robustness assessment.
articles.abstract: Radiomics analysis in PET offers a high-dimensional representation of tissue characteristics, yet its reliability is limited by sensitivity to acquisition perturbations, particularly dose reduction. This study aims to introduce a nonlinear stability phenotyping framework to characterize dose-response behavior of multi-organ radiomics and evaluate their potential relevance for future digital twin-oriented applications.Approach: A multi-center dataset of 550 total-body PET scans was analyzed. Dose reduction was simulated using list-mode subsampling (dose reduction factor - DRF = 2-100). A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted per organ. Stability was quantified using Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) and summarized as stability fractions. Nonlinear models were fitted to organ- and feature-level trajectories. Stability phenotypes and critical thresholds were derived, along with organ-level instability metrics.Main results: Radiomics stability exhibited strongly nonlinear, organ-dependent behavior. Feature-level analysis identified frequent sigmoid-associated collapse patterns with high descriptive model fits (R²>0.90). The liver showed the highest instability burden (30.8% unstable features), followed by esophagus and kidneys (18-20%). Texture features were the primary source of instability, whereas shape features remained robust. Organ-level trajectories demonstrated heterogeneous responses, with some organs maintaining high stability (0.80-0.95) across DRFs, while others showed sharp declines (down to 0.64). Linear (stable) behavior dominated at the organ level, though masking underlying nonlinear feature dynamics.Significance: Radiomics stability in total-body PET follows nonlinear, phenotype-driven dynamics with identifiable tipping points and organ-specific sensitivity. The proposed framework provides a behavior-based approach for evaluating radiomics robustness and supports the selection of reliable features and organs for robust quantitative imaging and may inform future digital twin-oriented applications.

articles.title: Integrating DWI Parameters with RECIST 1.1 for Early Assessment of Systemic Therapy Response in Lung Cancer Pelvic Bone Metastases.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To determine preliminary quantitative ADC thresholds for functional response and to evaluate whether integrating DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 provides complementary information for early systemic therapy response assessment in bone metastases. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included lung cancer patients with pelvic bone metastases who underwent three MRIs between November 2015 and November 2023: baseline, early time point (<4 months, TP1), and late (6-15 months, TP2) time points. ROC analysis based on lesion size change at TP2 determined ADC thresholds defining DWI response. A DWI response was defined as ADC >1300 µm²/s or ΔADC >0.14. An integrated response scheme (DWI-RECIST) combined this DWI-based response with RECIST assessment. Early responses at TP1 were compared between RECIST and DWI-RECIST using RECIST at TP2 as reference standard. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using net reclassification improvement and AUCs. RESULTS: Seventy-eight lesions from 27 patients were included. Compared with RECIST, DWI-RECIST yielded net classification gains of 7.4% (reader 1) and 11.1% (reader 2). DWI-RECIST showed higher AUCs than RECIST (reader 1: 0.6964 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.472; reader 2: 0.6415 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.781). Interobserver agreement for ADC was good (ICC 0.83-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ADC-derived DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 may provide complementary information for early assessment of pelvic bone metastases from lung cancer, particularly in lesions categorised as stable disease. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This pilot study proposes quantitative ADC thresholds and introduces a framework integrating these with RECIST 1.1 to support more objective response assessment in lung cancer pelvic bone metastases.

articles.title: Retrospective multi-reader evaluation of a Deep-Learning-based cancer detection model in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical impact of a deep-learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool applied to contrast-enhanced mammography on radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reading efficiency. METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study, 150 contrast-enhanced mammography examinations were interpreted by five radiologists. Each case was read and annotated twice in two sequential sessions: first without assistance and then with the computer-aided diagnostic tool, with a minimum 4-week washout period. Diagnostic performance was assessed at lesion and breast levels using free-response receiver operating characteristic analysis, area under the curve, and false-positive rate. Reading time for one radiologist was recorded as an exploratory measure. RESULTS: The computer-aided diagnostic tool was associated with improved lesion-level performance for most radiologists, with a mean increase in the area under the free-response curve of 0.030 ± 0.018. At 89% sensitivity, false-positive findings decreased by an average of 11.4% ± 24% across all radiologists. No improvement was observed at the breast level, possibly related to the tool's single-view analysis and dataset characteristics. An exploratory analysis showed a 31% reduction in reading time for one radiologist. CONCLUSION: Integration of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool into contrast-enhanced mammography was associated with improved lesion-level diagnostic performance and reduced false-positive findings, without measurable improvement at the breast level. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: To our knowledge, this study provides one of the early clinical evaluations of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool for contrast-enhanced mammography, suggesting potential improvements in lesion-level diagnostic performance and workflow efficiency while highlighting current limitations at the breast level.

articles.title: Why do authors publish radiological multivariable models: Questionnaire survey of motivations, evaluation, and usage in clinical practice.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Multivariable models currently comprise a large proportion of indexed radiological literature but authors' motivation to develop and publish models, available resource, plans for external evaluation, and whether models are used, is generally unknown. We aimed to answer these questions via a questionnaire survey. METHODS: We administered an online questionnaire to authors reporting multivariable prognostic or diagnostic models developed using regression, published in the top 3 indexed general radiological journals 2013 to 2015 and December 2022 to May 2023 inclusive. RESULTS: 34 authors responded. Regarding external evaluation, the most frequent response (49%, 17/35 responses) stated no intention to do this. Regarding barriers to evaluation, respondents cited lack of time (27%, 18/67 responses; multiple responses were possible), funding (22%, n = 15), and interest in development alone (19%, n = 13). 67% (n = 23) declared no or little statistical support. Most (82%, n = 28) did not use their own model in clinical practice and most (56%, n = 19) also believed other clinicians would not use the model either. Most (79%, n = 27) did not use models in general. A substantial proportion (29%, n = 10) reported model development to progress their career via publication. CONCLUSIONS: Most respondents had neither evaluated their model nor intended to do so. Most did not use their own model in clinical practice, nor did they believe others would. Statistical assistance was largely absent or minimal. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Our data suggest that the large volume of multivariable models currently available in the indexed medical literature have little clinical utility.

articles.title: QQ-Based Oxygen Extraction Fraction (OEF) Mapping in Mouse Brain: Initial Experience.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) is a vital biomarker of cerebral oxygen metabolism and tissue viability. A novel OEF mapping method, QQ, which combines quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) and quantitative blood oxygen level-dependent (qBOLD) (QSM + qBOLD = QQ), has demonstrated promise in detecting disease-related OEF abnormalities in humans. However, its application in preclinical mouse models remains untested. This study evaluates the feasibility and short-term within-session repeatability of the QQ method to capture physiological changes in the mouse brain. METHODS: In vivo MRI was performed on five C57BL/6 mice under four isoflurane anesthesia levels (1%, 1.5%, 2% and 2.5%). OEF maps were reconstructed using the QQ-CCTV algorithm. The relationship between anesthesia depth and OEF was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Repeatability was quantified via Bland-Altman plots and the within-subject coefficient of variation (CV). RESULTS: The QQ method generated relatively uniform OEF maps, capturing a significant, dose-dependent decrease in OEF with increasing isoflurane concentrations across the whole brain and targeted ROIs. Within-session repeatability of the QQ method was assessed at each isoflurane level using repeated-measures Bland-Altman analysis and the within-subject CV (9.7%-13.8%). CONCLUSION: This first application of the QQ method in the mouse brain demonstrates its feasibility for spatially resolved OEF quantification and lays the groundwork for future studies investigating oxygen metabolism in animal models.

articles.title: NR-MRC: A No-Reference Magnetic Resonance Curve Estimation Network for Tumor MR Image Quality Assessment and Enhancement.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate image quality assessment (IQA) is essential for evaluating tumor magnetic resonance (MR) images in clinical practice and computer-aided diagnosis. However, most existing IQA models are designed for natural images and require reference images for training. Variability in tissue characteristics, lesion location, and lesion morphology, together with the scarcity of high-quality MR reference images, makes quality assessment of tumor MR images particularly challenging. METHODS: To address these challenges, we propose a no-reference magnetic resonance curve estimation network named NR-MRC. First, a magnetic resonance curve estimation module uses nonlinear curve mapping to estimate spatially adjusted intensity and detail features without requiring reference tumor MR images. Second, a multi-scale feature estimation module extracts contextual features at different scales and fuses them with the initial estimates to generate enhanced MR images. Finally, a magnetic resonance scene statistics blind quality model evaluates feature consistency between the original images and their enhanced counterparts. RESULTS: Experiments on publicly available brain tumor and bladder cancer datasets demonstrate that NR-MRC outperforms the compared IQA and image enhancement methods. In the tested U-Net and DeepLab v3 settings, training with images selected by high NR-MRC scores or enhanced by NR-MRC increased segmentation metrics by approximately 20%. These task-specific gains do not by themselves establish improved clinical diagnostic image quality. CONCLUSION: NR-MRC provides no-reference quality assessment and enhancement for tumor MR images and shows potential utility in the evaluated downstream segmentation tasks.

articles.title: Frozen Echocardiography Foundation Model Embeddings Contain Linearly Recoverable LVOT VTI and TAPSE Report-Label Signal in MIMIC-IV-ECHO.
articles.abstract: Quantitative transthoracic echocardiographic measurements support cardiovascular assessment, but structured report-label values may be unavailable for downstream research. We evaluated whether frozen EchoPrime study-level embeddings encoded signal associated with structured left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LVOT VTI) and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) report-label values. MIMIC-IV-ECHO studies with report labels and frozen EchoPrime embeddings were analyzed. Clip-level 512-dimensional embeddings were mean-pooled into study-level all-clips embeddings. Supervised Ridge regression used deterministic subject-level train/validation/test splits, train-fit standardization, and validation-only alpha selection. LVOT VTI was primary, TAPSE secondary. Comparators were a train-median null model and leakage-safe non-image baselines using age, sex, and acquisition metadata. For LVOT VTI, 3782 studies were split into 2654 training, 573 validation, and 555 test studies. Ridge achieved test mean absolute error (MAE) 3.64 cm versus 4.54 cm for null, root mean squared error (RMSE) 4.66 cm, R2 0.372, and MAE 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.41-3.88 cm. Observed-vs-predicted Pearson r was 0.613 (95% CI, 0.556-0.664). For TAPSE, 1131 studies were split into 787 training, 184 validation, and 160 test studies. Ridge achieved MAE 3.17 mm versus 3.79 mm for null, RMSE 3.94 mm, R2 0.284, and MAE 95% CI 2.80-3.56 mm. Pearson r was 0.539 (95% CI, 0.424-0.632). Non-image baselines were weaker than imaging embeddings. Frozen EchoPrime study-level embeddings encoded signal associated with structured LVOT VTI and TAPSE report-label values. Findings support representation-level report-label prediction experiments, not EchoPrime fine-tuning, direct measurement extraction, measurement replacement, clinical deployment, or decision support.

articles.title: PW-GAN: Pseudo-Warping Field Guided GAN for Unsupervised Denoising of Fetal Brain MRI Images.
articles.abstract: Fetal brain MRI commonly uses thick-slice acquisitions to mitigate motion artifacts and preserve in-plane image quality. Multiple motion-corrupted stacks of 2D slices can be retrospectively reconstructed into isotropic 3D volumes; however, volumes reconstructed from thicker slices generally exhibit lower image quality than those reconstructed from thinner slices because limited through-plane information results in residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. Existing post-reconstruction denoising methods are limited by their dependence on large-scale datasets comprising noisy-clean image pairs or insufficient modeling of inter-slice structural consistency. In this work, we propose a Pseudo-Warping Field Guided Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Network (PW-GAN), which formulates post-reconstruction denoising as unpaired translation between low- and high-quality MRI domains. By incorporating a pseudo-warping field module, our method significantly enhances inter-slice continuity in the reconstructed volumes while effectively suppressing residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. On simulated data, PW-GAN achieved a PSNR of 39.65 dB and an SSIM of 0.9932. On real clinical data, it reduced the inter-slice warping error by up to 40% compared with unsupervised baselines. These results demonstrate that PW-GAN outperforms existing unsupervised models and achieves performance comparable to several state-of-the-art supervised methods. Qualitatively, PW-GAN produced cleaner results with smoother inter-slice structural transitions while preserving anatomical structures, demonstrating its effectiveness in post-reconstruction denoising of fetal brain MRI acquired from thick-slice scans.

articles.title: The Performance Ceiling of LIDC-IDRI Is Label-Defined Rather than Image-Defined: A Computable Bound and a Purposive Audit of Published Studies.
articles.abstract: Benchmarks labelled by panels of human readers underpin most medical image analysis. We ask whether such a dataset has a single attainable ceiling. All 1319 annotation files of the Lung Image Database Consortium image collection (LIDC-IDRI) were parsed into 7034 reader-level ratings. Modelling each nodule by a latent malignancy propensity of which the four reader verdicts are conditionally independent draws, we prove that no image-based model can exceed, against a reader-derived label, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the propensity itself; we derive how that bound depends on the labelling policy, test the independence assumption against a prediction the fit does not use, simulate its failures, and audit a purposive sample of 22 published studies against the rules they declare. Among 905 nodules read by all four radiologists, all four agreed exactly for 11.7% and 58.0% carried ratings spanning two or more points. Across three latent families, retaining every nodule the ceiling is 0.898-0.913; discarding the 19.6% the readers split two-two lifts it to 0.946-0.954; retaining only unanimous nodules discards 57.7% and lifts it to 0.991-0.994. On the binary scale, no family predicted more reader agreement than observed; simulated reader heterogeneity would make these ceilings slightly low. Of 27 reported figures, 11 lie above the bound implied by the study's own declared rule, four beyond sampling error and two if modest heterogeneity is also allowed for. The ceiling is set by the label, not by the images.

articles.title: Automated MRI Series Classification Across Heterogeneous Datasets Using Limited Manual Annotation.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the smallest tested fraction of manually labeled training data required for a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) classifier to achieve satisfactory MRI series classification performance (macro-F1 ≥ 0.80) across five heterogeneous public MRI datasets using digital imaging and communications in medicine (DICOM) metadata, image data, or both. This retrospective study included 3804 examinations and 14,054 MRI series from five public DICOM datasets spanning brain, knee, lumbar spine, liver, and breast MRI, accessed February-April 2026. AI classification models included a random forest classifier using DICOM header metadata, a deep convolutional neural network classifier using the geometric center slice of each MRI series, and decision-fusion models. Models were trained with 5%-40% of studies manually labeled in 5-percentage-point increments, with additional 1%-4% fractions for the knee and lumbar spine. Model performance was evaluated on the remaining studies using study-level splits across five random seeds. Results were summarized as mean ± standard deviation. Zero-label unsupervised clustering results were evaluated separately on the full dataset. The macro-F1 target was reached at the smallest tested training fraction of 1% in the lumbar spine (0.945 ± 0.013), at 2% in the knee (0.818 ± 0.006), at 10% in the brain (0.872 ± 0.027), and at 20% in the liver (0.827 ± 0.016) and the breast (0.847 ± 0.012). The best-performing model differed by dataset, reflecting different contributions from metadata versus image data. Across five separately evaluated public MRI datasets, at least one header-based, image-based, or combined model achieved macro-F1 ≥ 0.80 using no more than 20% manually labeled studies.

articles.title: Automated Multi-class Segmentation of Mandibular Odontogenic Cysts and the Mandibular Canal on CBCT Images Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework.
articles.abstract: Mandibular odontogenic cysts can complicate surgical planning if located near the mandibular canal. Accurate delineation of both structures is therefore clinically important. This study presents a deep learning-based method for simultaneously segmenting mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. The developed method relies on a hybrid deep learning architecture integrating a ConvNeXt-Base encoder, a Dilated Context Block, a U-Net-based decoder, and a Deep Supervision mechanism. This framework simultaneously segments the mandibular canal and odontogenic cyst regions within the same architecture, promoting multi-scale contextual feature learning. We evaluated the performance of the proposed method using fivefold cross-validation experiments on a real-world clinical CBCT dataset comprising 103 patient images. We assessed segmentation performance using overlap-based metrics together with boundary-aware HD95 and ASSD metrics. The experimental results demonstrated that the model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 76.28% ± 1.83%. Excluding the background class yielded macro IoU and macro F1-score values of 64.46% ± 2.74% and 77.00% ± 1.89%, respectively. Meanwhile, the weighted IoU and weighted F1-score values were 78.71% ± 4.25% and 87.63% ± 2.63%, respectively. In boundary-based evaluations, the mandibular canal had an HD95 of 2.44 ± 2.98 mm and an ASSD of 0.45 ± 0.30 mm. The corresponding values for odontogenic cysts were 5.59 ± 3.65 mm and 1.43 ± 0.88 mm, respectively. These results suggest that the mandibular canal is more consistently delineated, while cyst segmentation remains more challenging, particularly at irregular and low-contrast boundaries. The proposed framework allows for the simultaneous and objective segmentation of mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal within a unified, multi-class CBCT analysis framework. By providing reproducible delineation of both structures, this method could serve as a technical foundation for future quantitative analyses of lesion-canal relationships. However, further validation using larger, multicenter, volumetric CBCT datasets is required before clinical translation.

articles.title: Hair Segmentation and Skin Characterization on Macroscopic Dermatological Images for Laser Treatment Parameterization.
articles.abstract: Current light-based devices, such as laser hair removal, intense pulsed light (IPL), vascular laser therapy, and dermatologic phototherapy, are widely used in clinical dermatology but rely heavily on subjective manual parameterization or uncalibrated point-based colorimeters. To overcome these limitations, this work presents a unified system for hair segmentation and skin characterization in macroscopic dermatological images. Unlike most existing literature that relies on dermoscopic datasets captured under highly controlled conditions, our approach is specifically designed for macroscopic images that replicate real clinical laser treatments. The proposed pipeline integrates a custom-trained variant of the YOLOv9 deep learning architecture for instance segmentation and classical image processing within a single workflow to extract objective skin and hair parameters such as phototype, hair density, color, and thickness. A color calibration stage using spectrophotometric measurements ensures accurate feature estimation regardless of illumination conditions. Experimental results show competitive segmentation metrics (mAP@50 ≈ 0.80) on a custom dataset featuring short, shaved hairs, typical of pre-treatment scenarios. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed pipeline in providing the objective, foundational skin and hair features required for future automated laser parameterization, paving the way for its extension to broader light-based medical therapies.

articles.title: Annotation-Efficient Individual Muscle Segmentation from Dixon MRI: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark of Pretraining and Fat-Fraction Guidance.
articles.abstract: Measuring individual muscles and their fatty infiltration on Dixon MRI can support sarcopenia assessment, but manual annotation is time-consuming and annotated datasets are often small. This study investigated accurate individual-muscle segmentation with limited labelled data. Three datasets were used: an abdominal CT dataset of 300 subjects with adipose-tissue labels, a lower-limb Dixon MRI dataset of 25 subjects with 13 thigh and 9 calf muscles, and an independent cohort of 66 subjects for external testing. Network architecture, encoder pretraining, a Dixon-derived fat-fraction input, and a shared CT-MRI encoder were compared. A 2.5D model, subject-level cross-validation, zero-shot transfer, label-free domain adaptation, and few-shot adaptation were also evaluated. The best models reached Dice 0.947 ± 0.017  for CT adipose tissue and 0.925 ± 0.010  for thigh muscle; the best 2.5D model reached 0.928, while a reported 3D Attention-Res-V-Net reached 0.857 under a different protocol. Encoder pretraining helped most at the smallest budgets, with ImageNet performing best and comparably to CT-based pretraining at eight subjects. A shared CT-MRI encoder retained accuracy with 44 %  fewer parameters, and thigh-muscle volumes agreed closely with reference measurements (ICC ( 2 , 1 ) = 0.998  ). On the external cohort, fine-tuning raised Dice from 0.11 zero-shot to 0.61, 0.76, and 0.88 with four, eight, and 46 labelled target subjects. The fat-fraction input improved segmentation only when very few subjects (two or four) were labelled. Encoder pretraining and efficient model sharing help when annotated MRI data are scarce. A small amount of target-domain annotation substantially improves cross-cohort transfer, and repeated subject-level validation is important for reliable evaluation.

articles.title: BLIX-Ray: Chest X-Ray Report Generation with Vision-Language Models and Reinforcement Learning.
articles.abstract: The radiology report is essential for directing the course of treatment for a patient. However, writing radiology reports is a huge burden for radiologists. Manual reporting faces challenges due to intra-labeler and inter-labeler variability, causing inconsistent patient treatment and diagnostic results, and complicating matters due to alertness and changing judgment. To address these challenges, we propose an automated radiology report generation model tailored for chest X-ray imaging. We introduce BLIX-Ray, a vision-language model (VLM) designed to generate radiology reports using a transfer learning approach. BLIX-Ray fine-tunes the pre-trained BLIP model to extract and align rich visual and textual representations suited to the medical imaging domain. We use reinforcement learning (RL) to directly optimize report generation based on language evaluation metrics in order to further enhance performance. We evaluate BLIX-Ray on two publicly available datasets: IU-Xray and CheXpert Plus. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves the highest CIDEr and BERTScore on both datasets, while n-gram-oriented baselines retain an advantage on BLEU. BLIX-Ray integrates reinforcement learning and transfer learning to improve medical report generation under limited and heterogeneous data conditions. The results highlight the potential of vision-language models to support automated and standardized radiology reporting. Notably, BLIX-Ray achieves the best reported CIDEr (0.6534) and BERTScore (0.8765) among the compared methods on IU-Xray and leads on CIDEr, METEOR, and BERTScore on CheXpert Plus (BERTScore 0.8407), demonstrating strong report-level consensus and semantic similarity with the reference reports.

articles.title: Impact of Field Strength and Contrast Agents on Cardiac MRI Radiomic Features of the Myocardium and Blood Pool.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of gadolinium-based contrast agents on cardiac MRI radiomic features across different magnetic field strengths. With Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval, eight healthy volunteers (38.5 ± 15.4 years; 4 males) underwent four consecutive cardiac MRI examinations using a Modified Look-Locker Inversion Recovery (MOLLI) sequence at 1.5T and 3T, with and without two contrast agents, gadopentetate dimeglumine (Gd-DTPA), and gadofosveset trisodium. Radiomic features were extracted from the myocardium and blood pool at the mid-ventricular level of the left ventricle using the first raw MOLLI image, corresponding to the shortest inversion time. Before contrast administration, switching from 1.5 to 3 T resulted in significant changes in 52% of myocardial and 56% of blood pool radiomic features. Contrast administration further altered radiomic feature values. At 1.5T, Gd-DTPA altered 42% of myocardial and 63% of blood pool features, whereas gadofosveset altered 73% and 85%, respectively. Similar patterns were observed at 3 T, with gadofosveset producing a greater proportion of altered features than Gd-DTPA (p < 0.05). Blood pool features were generally more sensitive to contrast administration than myocardial features. At 10 min after contrast administration, significant differences between the two contrast agents were observed in 48% of myocardial and 23% of blood pool features at 1.5T and in 72% and 60%, respectively, at 3 T. In conclusion, the administration and type of gadolinium-based contrast agents significantly alter cardiac MRI radiomic features across different magnetic field strengths. Future research should prioritize normalization strategies and evaluate feature robustness across larger patient populations to enhance the generalizability of cardiac radiomics.

articles.title: SVF-net: A Dual-encoder Network with Adaptive Gated Fusion for Colorectal Polyp Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Automatic colorectal polyp segmentation in retrospective still colonoscopy images remains challenging for small, low-contrast, partially occluded, or irregular lesions. We propose SVF-Net, a heterogeneous dual-encoder network combining a frozen SAM2 Hiera-L image trunk with a trainable MaxViT-RMLP-Small specialist branch. At four feature scales, the two streams are projected to a common width, spatially aligned, and reconciled by complementary channel-spatial gating before progressive decoding. Across five public benchmarks, three-run mean mDice is 0.922 on CVC-ClinicDB, 0.898 on Kvasir-SEG, 0.805 on CVC-ColonDB, 0.770 on ETIS-LaribPolypDB, and 0.896 on CVC-300. Matched projected-concatenation and fixed-weight ( G = 0.5  ) controls retain the surrounding fusion path while removing input-dependent weighting; across ten matched training runs, adaptive gating gives higher mean mDice than both controls on all five datasets. Dataset-wide gate diagnostics on all 380 CVC-ColonDB and 196 ETIS cases indicate non-collapsed, scale- and region-dependent activations, while targeted one-factor sensitivity checks cover the MaxViT learning-rate multiplier, gate initialization, and auxiliary-loss weight. Matched per-case analyses further show that cross-domain gains are heterogeneous across lesion size, brightness, and an image-derived specular-reflection proxy. SVF-Net requires 92.8 ms per image (10.8 FPS) and 8.5 GB peak GPU memory on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 under the reported profiling protocol. The study evaluates retrospective static images only and does not establish real-time colonoscopy performance, prospective clinical effectiveness, or clinician benefit.

articles.title: Wavelet Scalogram-Based Nystagmus Classification for Automated Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo Subtype Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is the most common cause of vestibular vertigo, yet accurate diagnosis remains challenging without specialist expertise. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic algorithm for BPPV using video-nystagmography (VNG) recordings. A total of 1352 VNG recordings were collected from patients with posterior semicircular canal (PSCC) BPPV (n = 234), lateral semicircular canal (LSCC) BPPV (canalolithiasis, n = 188; cupulolithiasis, n = 58), and healthy controls (n = 224) at a single tertiary referral hospital, yielding 1738 signal segments (1312 nystagmus segments annotated by two otolaryngologists and 426 normal segments). Eye trajectory signals were extracted using a deep learning-based VNG eye-tracking algorithm, transformed into two-dimensional (2D) scalogram representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT), and classified using task-specific backbone architectures selected through systematic comparison under a patient-level data split. Ablation analysis showed that CWT-based 2D representations significantly outperformed raw one-dimensional (1D) time-series baselines. The final models achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values of 0.974 for horizontal and 0.961 for torsional nystagmus classification. For BPPV subtype diagnosis, recording-level accuracy was 0.935 for the PSCC and 0.938 for the LSCC evaluation; F1-scores exceeded 0.84 for all PSCC classes and ranged from 0.59 to 0.98 for LSCC classes, with canalolithiasis variants outperforming cupulolithiasis variants. These findings suggest the feasibility of AI-assisted BPPV diagnosis from VNG recordings.

articles.title: Access Vessel Patency After Endovascular Therapy via Tibiopedal Access in Patients With Lower Extremity Artery Disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the access vessel patency after endovascular therapy performed via tibiopedal access. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center, observational study. Patients who underwent endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access with sheath insertion were enrolled. The primary outcome was loss of access vessel patency defined as access vessel occlusion or stenosis with a peak systolic velocity ratio > 2.4 on duplex ultrasound at 6 months. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the predictors of access vessel patency loss, with hemodialysis, severely calcified access vessel and sheath-to-artery ratio included as covariates. RESULTS: A total of 95 limbs in 91 patients were included in this study, and loss of access vessel patency was observed in 22 limbs (23.1%). Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that sheath-to-artery ratio was the only independent predictor (odds ratio: 1.493, 95% confidence interval: 1.130-1.976; p = 0.005). The receiver operating characteristic curve analysis revealed that the optimal cutoff value of sheath-to-artery ratio for predicting loss of access vessel patency was 1.08, with an area under the curve of 0.723. In this cohort, the 2-year freedom from major adverse limb events were 98.6% (95% CI: 90.8-99.8%), and no major amputation occurred. CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrated a relatively high incidence of loss of access vessel patency after endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access, although this was not associated with an increase in major adverse limb events. A larger sheath-to-artery ratio was identified as an independent predictor of loss of access vessel patency.

articles.title: Technique, Safety and Adoption of Genicular Artery Embolization for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Nationwide Analysis of the German Quality-Assurance Registry.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the nationwide adoption of genicular artery embolization (GAE) in Germany and to describe patient selection, technique, safety and radiation dose. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed procedures recorded in the quality-assurance registry of the German Society for Interventional Radiology and Minimally Invasive Therapy (DeGIR), from January 2024 to December 2025. Technical success, entered per procedure, was defined as subjective adequate devascularization of the synovial blush. Complications were graded using the modified CIRSE classification, and radiation exposure was expressed as dose-area product (DAP) and fluoroscopy time. The analysis was primarily descriptive. RESULTS: Overall, 2335 procedures in 2209 patients across 109 centers in 15 federal states were recorded (median age 67 years, IQR 59-77; 57% female; prior total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in 300, 13%). Annual volume rose from 579 procedures in 2024 to 1,756 in 2025, and the embolic agent shifted from permanent (40-21%) toward temporary microspheres (4-29%). Center-reported technical success was 93% (87% in 2024, 94% in 2025). Eleven complications were recorded (0.5%), all CIRSE grade 1-3, with no permanent sequelae; none were recorded in 2024. Median DAP was 1536 cGy cm2 (IQR 731-3048) and median fluoroscopy time 24 min (IQR 16-34). CONCLUSION: During rapid nationwide adoption, GAE was performed for osteoarthritis-related and post-TKA pain with low radiation dose and high center-reported technical success across centers of all volumes, supporting its feasibility in routine practice. The complication rate is a lower limit, as the registry is not designed for complication surveillance.

articles.title: Cost Analysis of Percutaneous Segmentectomy Versus Chemoembolisation and Radioembolisation in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the costs of percutaneous segmentectomy, a single-session combination of transarterial embolisation and microwave ablation, against chemoembolisation and radioembolisation for hepatocellular carcinoma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cost analysis of 66 patients treated with percutaneous segmentectomy at five Italian centres, using bottom-up micro-costing. Comparator costs were derived from published Italian per-session costs multiplied by mean sessions per patient, and survival from published curves. A partitioned survival model estimated life-years and incremental net monetary benefit at 50,000 euros per life-year. RESULTS: Procedural cost per treated patient was 6331 euros for percutaneous segmentectomy, 9792 euros for chemoembolisation (mean 2.94 sessions), and 21,673 euros for radioembolisation (1.52 sessions). At 24 months, percutaneous segmentectomy had lower total cost and a small life-year deficit (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio approximately 70,800 euros per life-year versus chemoembolisation and 57,500 versus radioembolisation, both above threshold). This life-year-adjusted advantage reversed versus chemoembolisation, and became neutral versus radioembolisation, in a worst-case sensitivity analysis, and reversed against both when transplantation costs for the eight transplanted patients (19%) were attributed to percutaneous segmentectomy alone. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, percutaneous segmentectomy appeared to have a lower procedural cost per treated patient than chemoembolisation and radioembolisation, mainly because it is delivered in a single session. However, because costing routes, cohorts, and survival sources were not equivalent and the life-year-adjusted comparison was not robust, no formal cost superiority can be established. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective, matched studies. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Retrospective Cohort Study with Historical Comparators.

articles.title: Perfusion characterization of osteosarcoma spinal metastases using advanced T1-weighted dynamic contrast enhanced MRI.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Spinal osteosarcoma is rare and highly aggressive malignancy associated with poor clinical outcomes. To our knowledge, the perfusion MRI features of spinal osteosarcoma using T1-weighted DCE MRI, including plasma volume, permeability, and time-intensity analysis, have not previously been studied. In addition, changes in these features following radiation treatment have not yet been evaluated. We hypothesize that highly malignant spinal osteosarcoma demonstrates hypervascularity based on its pharmacokinetic perfusion parameters. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed 27 patients (mean age 44.5, SD 21.8) of untreated metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma who underwent DCE-MRI. Perfusion parameters, including Ktrans and plasma volume (Vp) as an indicator of permeability and tumor vascularity respectively, were measured using the extended Tofts model. A subset of 12 patients underwent preradiation therapy (RT), 18F-FDG PET, and 7 patients had post-RT DCE-MRI for assessment of treatment effects. Additionally, time intensity curve analysis was conducted to evaluate post-treatment changes. RESULTS: Thirty-five lesions in 27 patients were evaluated. Perfusion characteristics including mean Ktrans and Vp were 0.323 and 3.54, respectively, indicating that metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma is hypervascular. In the 7 patients with post-RT DCE-MRI, the mean post-RT Vp decreased to 1.77 from a pre-RT mean of 3.28, reflecting a 46.04% decrease to radiation therapy. CONCLUSION: DCE-MRI evaluation of metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma demonstrates a rich blood supply, consistent with hypervascular metastatic disease. Changes in the time intensity curve analysis may serve as non-invasive marker of radiation treatment response.

articles.title: Ganglioneuroma of the sacral canal: an unusual location with MR imaging findings.
articles.abstract: Ganglioneuroma is a rare, benign, slow-growing tumor arising from embryonic neural crest cells that differentiate into the sympathetic ganglia. Accordingly, it can occur anywhere along the sympathetic chain, from the clivus to the sacrum, although it is seen most commonly in the mediastinum, retroperitoneum, adrenal glands, and neck. Although involvement at the sacral level is uncommon, ganglioneuroma typically arises from the anterior surface of the sacrum, with presacral lesions occasionally extending through the sacral foramina into the sacral canal. Only two cases of ganglioneuroma confined to the sacral canal without presacral involvement have been reported in the literature, to the best our knowledge. On magnetic resonance imaging, ganglioneuroma usually demonstrates a low signal intensity on T1-weighted images, heterogeneous high signal intensity on T2-weighted images, and variable enhancement patterns. We report a case of sacral canal ganglioneuroma in a 72-year-old woman presenting with a fluid level which is a previously unreported imaging feature, to the best of our knowledge. The unusual patient age, location, and imaging characteristics of this patient's ganglioneuroma posed a diagnostic challenge. We also review previously reported cases of sacral canal ganglioneuroma and highlight the radiologic features, with particular emphasis on the presence of a fluid level.

articles.title: A review of Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for medical image analysis.
articles.abstract: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) replace selected scalar weights or fixed activations with learnable univariate edge functions. We conducted a controlled retrospective evidence reconstruction and update of Crossref, Europe PMC, arXiv, and OpenAlex, supplemented by local full texts and citation tracking, for studies published from January 2024 to February 2026. After report-level screening and version consolidation, 138 independent medical-imaging studies met explicitly defined medical-imaging eligibility criteria (127 direct imaging inputs; 11 image-derived representations). Studies were classified by primary KAN placement - backbone, bottleneck/token, physics-informed or implicit representation, or task-specific head - and evaluated for task, modality, comparator, reported result, and evidence of a KAN-specific contribution. None met the strictest contribution-evidence standard of a complete resource-controlled factorial comparison; 48 provided moderate, 46 weak/compound, and 44 insufficient evidence for the independent KAN contribution. Whole-model results were favorable in 68 studies, mixed or trade-off in 30, unfavorable or without incremental gain in 4, and indeterminate or not comparable in 36; these labels do not isolate the effect of KAN. External validation, calibration, repeated-run stability, and deployment metrics were inconsistently reported. The evidence supports KAN chiefly as a task-dependent module for controlled testing within established convolutional, Transformer, state-space, or physics-informed pipelines, rather than as a generally superior replacement. Priorities include matched ablations, function-stability analysis, external-center evaluation, and standardized resource reporting.

articles.title: Blunt traumatic injuries of the craniocervical junction in adults; appearances on cross-sectional imaging.
articles.abstract: Blunt traumatic injuries of the craniocervical junction (CCJ) comprise an important subset of cervical spine injuries associated with high morbidity and mortality. An anatomical understanding of the CCJ, as well as a sound knowledge of the appearances of CCJ injuries on multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), are crucial to determine the degree and extent of pathology and guide clinical management. In this article we review the cross-sectional imaging features of blunt traumatic CCJ injuries in adults, highlighting the relevant CCJ anatomy and using illustrative cases from our major trauma centres.

articles.title: Development and validation of a U-Net-based deep learning model for automatic measurement of the hallux valgus angle and intermetatarsal angle.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate a U-Net-based deep learning model for the automated measurement of the hallux valgus angle (HVA) and intermetatarsal angle (IMA) on weight-bearing dorsoplantar foot radiographs and to compare model performance with expert reference values. METHODS: A total of 1227 weight-bearing dorsoplantar radiographs were obtained. The dataset was divided into training (n = 858), validation (n = 184), and testing (n = 185) datasets. Data augmentation was applied to the training set, yielding 10,296 samples. Six anatomical landmark points were labeled to define the axes of the proximal phalanges of the hallux, and of the first and second metatarsal. For temporal validation, 100 additional radiographs obtained at the same institution were evaluated. The U-Net-based model measurements were compared with the median values obtained from three independent experts (two foot and ankle surgeons and one musculoskeletal radiologist). RESULTS: In the temporal validation cohort, the AI model demonstrated high agreement with the expert reference standard. For the HVA, the mean absolute error (MAE) was 2.118° (95% CI: 1.770-2.475) and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) was 0.961. For the IMA, the MAE was 0.966° (95% CI: 0.809-1.133) and the ICC was 0.919. Subgroup analysis revealed that the accuracy remained consistent across mild, moderate, and severe deformities. CONCLUSION: The proposed U-Net-based model provided accurate and reproducible automatic measurements of the HVA and IMA on weight-bearing dorsoplantar foot radiographs with high agreement with expert reference values. This approach may serve as a practical tool for standardized radiographic assessment of hallux valgus in clinical practice and research.
